name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=render/graphics, descriptor=circle_anim_row). Accurately reflects the body: it renders one horizontal scanline ('row') per loop iteration for a filled-circle band animation. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix tied to 0x219ad or any data address). Confirmed semantics from both callers: it always iterates a row range painting circle slices.
purpose: Render the horizontal slices of a filled-circle (band) animation across a row range, palette-remapping a sprite-sourced run into the battle render workspace one scanline at a time.
logic_summary: for each row in [start_row, end_row): if the row lies strictly inside the circle's vertical extent (cy-r, cy+r): dy=abs(cy-row); rsq_minus_dy2 = r*r - dy*dy; half_width = trunc(sqrt(rsq_minus_dy2) * scale_num / 10.0) (x87 forces round-toward-zero via __CHP before FRNDINT, so this truncates -- the Ghidra ROUND() macro is misleading). Left edge = cx-half_width clamped to 0 (carrying right_off=cx when clamped); right edge clamped so cx+half_width <= 0x138. Then fd2_apply_palette_remap_run(palette_remap_src, right_off+half_width, dst) where dst = large_game_state_buffer + 0x8088 + row*0x1C8 + left_clip. 0x8088=char-layer base in render workspace, 0x1C8=456 pitch, 0x138=312 visible clipped width.
signature: void fd2_render_circle_anim_row(int cx, int cy, int r, int scale_num, int start_row, int end_row, uint8 *palette_remap_src)

params.name: cx
params.semantics: Circle center column (X pixel coordinate); used as the scanline's horizontal center for left/right edge computation and clipping against 0..0x138.
params.reason: Standard, accurate name for the horizontal center; no address residue.

params.name: cy
params.semantics: Circle center row (Y pixel coordinate); used to compute dy=abs(cy-row) and the vertical-extent test (cy-r, cy+r).
params.reason: Standard, accurate name for the vertical center; no address residue.

params.name: r
params.semantics: Circle radius; defines both the vertical extent bounds and r*r in the half-width formula.
params.reason: Standard radius name; no address residue.

params.name: scale_num
params.semantics: Scale-factor numerator multiplied with sqrt(r*r-dy*dy) before dividing by the fixed 10.0 divisor; shapes the band thickness/curvature. Callers pass 0xC (rising-sparkle pre-cast effect) and 0x10 (filled-circle band).
params.reason: Accurately describes its role as the numerator in the half-width scaling; confirmed by caller-passed constants 0xC and 0x10; no address residue.

params.name: start_row
params.semantics: Inclusive starting scanline index of the loop (ESI start).
params.reason: Accurate loop-start name; no address residue.

params.name: end_row
params.semantics: Exclusive ending scanline index of the loop (loop runs while start_row < end_row).
params.reason: Accurate exclusive-end name; no address residue.

params.name: palette_remap_src
params.semantics: Per-frame sprite/palette-remap source row pointer, passed straight through as the 1st argument to fd2_apply_palette_remap_run.
params.reason: Accurately describes the pass-through palette-remap source; no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; renders into the global render workspace as a side effect. (Original tail-jumps to a shared Watcom epilogue; the C equivalent is the loop simply running to completion.)

notes: Source comment block (lines 994-1033) is already precise, ASCII, and fully consistent with the decompilation and plate: it correctly documents the truncation (not round-to-nearest), the clamp behavior, the dst layout (0x8088/0x1C8/0x138), the caller-passed scale_num values (0xC/0x10), and the tail-jump-shared-epilogue exit. No Edit needed. Ghidra plate is more verbose (asm-level FILD/FMULP/FDIV/__CHP/FRNDINT/FISTP detail, exact callee/caller addresses) but does not contradict the src conclusion, so the plate was left unchanged. Confirmed both callers: fd2_play_rising_pre_cast_effect passes scale_num=0xc, fd2_render_filled_circle_band_anim passes 0x10 at both sites. No logic changes made.
